sources.title: Knecht inspected source README
sources.locator: README.md Features, Hosting, Install on macOS, Pre-releases and License
sources.finding: The pinned main repository documents a browser dashboard, self-hosted Linux/Docker or Mac/Lima installation, one DDEV environment per run, GitHub PR output and FSL-1.1-ALv2 licensing with an Apache future license.

sources.title: Knecht official introduction
sources.locator: What Is Knecht; What Knecht Is Not; Features
sources.finding: The product is a self-hosted workflow dashboard: deterministic steps and optional AI run in project containers. It supports server cron, issue/Git events, follow-up prompts, previews and team sign-in. The vendor operates only a limited beta-instance program rather than an unrestricted managed-cloud service.

sources.title: Knecht actual agent/runtime/auth documentation
sources.locator: AI Agent opening; Where It Runs; Models; AI Connection per Project; Follow-Ups and Mentions
sources.finding: The AI step starts OpenCode in a project web container with a provider key. The agent runs as non-root, with no Docker socket/DDEV CLI exposure, separate environment network, provider key in the process environment and repository-scoped short-lived Git credentials. Global/project keys/models are separate; smaller subtask delegation belongs to the underlying agent.

sources.title: Knecht concrete OpenCode configuration
sources.finding: The pinned implementation builds an OpenCode configuration with a model, optional small_model, instructions, MCP servers and provider API key read from KNECHT_AI_KEY. This is OpenCode coding-agent integration, not evidence that every underlying provider model is a separate coding harness.

sources.title: Knecht ACP agent-session wrapper
sources.finding: The implementation wraps one launched agent process as one ACP session and extracts tool-change old/new text for the transcript. The actual OpenCode identity is established by the agent documentation/configuration; this generic wrapper alone is not used to name other harnesses.

sources.title: Knecht product trigger semantics
sources.locator: Triggers, Issue Trackers; How Triggers Behave; Schedule
sources.finding: Product-owned triggers accept GitHub or linked issue-tracker events and cron. Same-issue/session runs serialize; independent environments can run separately. Cron uses server local time and fires once after an outage rather than replaying every missed slot. Trigger inputs retain issue identifier/title/body/URL and event metadata.

sources.title: Knecht workflow and Git output steps
sources.locator: Workflows opening; Run Variables; Reporting Back; Workflows as Code example
sources.finding: A workflow has sequential steps with no parallel branches. Documented native steps create a branch, create a commit and open a PR, and external-trigger inputs/issue session context flow into the run.

sources.title: Knecht GitHub integration
sources.locator: Setup; Issue Events and Conditions; Workflow Steps
sources.finding: The GitHub App handles repository sign-in/access and events. Native workflow steps create commits under the app bot, push a branch and open a PR against the project default branch, adding a preview URL and a dashboard Open Pull Request action.

sources.title: Knecht displayed inline code diff
sources.locator: app/components/chat/ToolRow.vue diffLines computation and open item.diff template
sources.finding: The actual browser ToolRow component derives old/new line differences and displays each complete line.text with a+/- marker when the user expands a diff-bearing tool result. The content-rendering interface is inspected directly; backend diff metadata or file counts alone are not the proof.

sources.title: Knecht beta operation and credits
sources.locator: Beta Testers, Managed or Self-Hosted; Getting Your OpenCode Credit
sources.finding: The docs call this a closed beta. Managed instances are vendor-operated and limited; self-hosted instances use the same software/setup and are unlimited. Beta OpenCode credit is delivered as a capped workspace key, not a personal OpenCode subscription or unlimited ongoing free tier.

sources.title: Knecht Functional Source License
sources.locator: LICENSE.md FSL-1.1-ALv2 grant, Permitted Purpose and Future License
sources.finding: The main software is FSL-1.1-ALv2, allowing internal and other permitted uses while restricting competing commercial services. Each version changes to Apache-2.0 after its stated two-year future-license period; it is not Apache-2.0 today merely because that is the future license.
